correctness.evidence: Clean-room direct hook-length scans over all partitions through the classical pair-core maximum-size bounds 15 and 35 reproduced exactly the claimed 10 and 21 objects, size distributions, maximizers, beta-sets, Durfee data, and maximum-witness hook multisets.

originality.evidence: Exact-table searches did not locate prior full 10-object or 21-object tables with the claimed metadata. Credit is narrow: Yang–Zhong–Zhou arXiv:1406.2583 already gives general number/maximum results for (s,s+1,s+2)-cores, so the (5,6,7) aggregate facts are not new.

value.evidence: After subtracting known general results, the residual contribution is a routine explicit census of 10 and 21 objects using classical core criteria, without a general formula, structural theorem, meaningful new regime, or algorithmic advance.

literature.title: On the Enumeration of (s,s+1,s+2)-Core Partitions
literature.authors: Jane Y. X. Yang; Michael X. X. Zhong; Robin D. P. Zhou
literature.coverage: General enumeration and maximum-size results for consecutive triples; s=5 covers the aggregate (5,6,7) facts.

literature.title: Olsson–Stanton pair-core maximum theorem (as summarized in later literature)
literature.coverage: For coprime s,t, maximum (s,t)-core size is (s^2-1)(t^2-1)/24, giving exhaustive scan bounds 15 for (4,5) and 35 for (5,6).

repair.reason: Reframing the finite lists as examples/fixtures is accurate but does not meet the campaign's scientific-value criterion; rescue would require a substantive parameterized theorem or structural generalization.

final_reason: The enumerations are correct and the explicit tables were not found in the searched sources, but the residual content is too small and routine to constitute a scientifically valuable independent finding.
